# Lexer errors (PHEL300-399)

The lexer turns source text into tokens. A code in this range means the file holds a character or a literal the language does not accept.

| Code | Error |
|---|---|
| [PHEL301](#phel301-unterminated-string) | Unterminated string |
| [PHEL310](#phel310-lexer-error) | Lexer error |

## PHEL301: Unterminated string

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNTERMINATED_STRING`

A `"` opens a string that no later `"` closes. The lexer hands the rest to the atom rule, and the parser reports it at the opening quote.

```phel
"abc
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `"`, or escape the quote you meant to keep as `\"`.

## PHEL310: Lexer error

Enum case: `ErrorCode::LEXER_ERROR`

No token rule matches the source at that position. A bare `#` is the usual cause: every `#` form needs the character that follows it.

```phel
(inc #)
```

**Fix:** Delete the stray character, or complete the reader form it starts.
